problem: The lines b.onclick = pay; and b.removeEventListener('click', pay); use the symbols b and pay without saying what they stand for, so a first-time reader has to guess.
fix: Introduce them: 'let b = document.getElementById('payBtn'); and a named function pay() { ... }. Then b.onclick = pay; stores that one function in the property.'

problem: The capture phase is described as running 'from window down to the target's parent', which leaves it unclear what happens to a listener added with {capture:true} on the target itself (it runs in the target phase, in registration order with the ordinary listeners). Readers can be confused when the capture listener sits on the clicked element.
fix: Add one sentence: 'A capture listener placed on the target itself does not run early; on the target, all its listeners run in the target phase, in the order they were added, whatever their capture flag.'

where: Section 3 table, scroll and resize rows
problem: The chapter teaches that bubbling makes delegation work, but scroll and resize listeners do not bubble from elements; a student may try to delegate them on a parent and see nothing fire.
fix: In the scroll row, note: 'scroll on an element does not bubble; attach it to that element itself or set capture:true. resize fires on window.'

problem: 'Value is committed' does not say that change fires only if the value actually changed since the field gained focus; a student may expect a log on every blur.
fix: Write: 'change | value is committed and differs from the value when the field got focus; text input loses focus or gets Enter, select fires immediately | validate a field'
